actions.action: Embed once, then one development run, then the gate. 'python -m src.train --embed-only' is started as soon as steps 6-9 are complete; every later run embeds nothing. The development run grid-searches R4 (linear, C in 0.3 and 1, rule weight in 0.3 and 1.0) on family folds plus 5 grouped folds, fits R1-R3 at R4's setting, and runs three report-only folds (yanis alone, aya alone, jackhhao alone held out). Gate constants are fixed in code before the run; all use development data and the gate asserts that no test row reaches it. G1: pooled over official_dev, handwritten_dev and handwritten_dev3 (661 texts), false alarms and misses not above the champion's, read from report/round3/dev_scores.csv. G2: official_dev counted by payload group with tolerance 0, the two hand-written sets with tolerance 1 text. G3: on family-held-out folds no new benign source has more false alarms than the champion on the same texts and at most 2%, and total misses on new attack sources are lower. G4: on the 'check' halves of the probe slices plus real_action_dev, pooled benign false alarms not above the champion's and misses lower; differences of one row on sets under 60 rows count as equal; the known miss is flagged; on benign command rows where the rule is silent the median calibrated probability rises by at most 0.10. G5: false alarms on non-English hard negatives not more than 1 point above English hard negatives, unsupported-language probe at most 5%. The comparison with the REPLICA baseline per source is advisory. Promotion: the highest rung that passes and is not worse than the rung below by 2 or more rows pooled; if that rung is not R4 its full grid is run before saving; promotion uses os.replace; if nothing passes the champion stays. One repair run is allowed (tighten or drop a rule, add more varied benign rows); then the result stands.
actions.verify: Second '--embed-only' reports 0 new pieces and the first 39,027 cache rows are unchanged. Gate self-tests without training: challenger = champion gives all differences 0; champion with threshold -1.0 is rejected and the model file hash is unchanged. After the run report/gate.json lists only development set names, every count and the reason; the promoted file's sha256 equals the candidate named there; re-scoring the development sets and the long probe texts through predict() reproduces the gate's verdicts.
actions.cost: Machine: embedding 25-45 minutes once; development run about 1.5-2 hours (roughly 95-110 fits on folds of about 30,000 units); a repair run about 1-1.5 hours more.

actions.action: Robustness measurement and the retraining path, development data only. scripts/robustness_check.py: burial check on a sample of about 60 caught development attacks at 3 positions and 5 document lengths (2,000 to 30,000 characters), carriers built from benign rows the scoring model did not train on, reported separately for attacks with and without a rule hit, with false alarms on the same documents without payload. Retraining: optional data/feedback_train.csv (appended last in load_pool, case id used as group, excluded from leave-one-source-out while small) and data/regression_dev.csv (reported text, at least two rewordings and one harmless look-alike held out per case); scripts/add_example.py refuses near-copies of test rows, warns at similarity 0.6 against development rows and prints which variants the pool filter would remove; 'python -m src.train --quick' reuses the saved parameters, runs the 5 grouped folds only and goes through the same gate in src/gate.py. The per-family unseen-style table (unweighted mean and range, original rows) is written each round.
actions.verify: Burial table exists for both groups and all lengths; the caller-side split length stated in the write-up is the length this table supports. Dry run of the retraining path with a development miss that round four does not target: held-out rewordings flagged, held-out look-alike not flagged, quick run time measured and recorded, gate passes.
actions.cost: About 1.5 days of work. Machine: burial check 10-15 minutes, quick retrain to be measured (expected 10-20 minutes).

actions.action: Freeze, then score the sealed sets once. 'python -m src.evaluate --freeze' writes report/frozen.json: sha256 of the promoted model and of src/rules.py, rules_r3.py, normalize.py, windows.py, pipeline.py, features.py, predict.py, the limits, the embedding model name, the standards, expected ranges taken from the family-held-out folds, and the pre-declared probes (false alarms on non-English benign text, results by length bucket, false alarms on harmless texts containing an address, 'sudo' or 'rm -rf'; toxic-chat recall split into positives with and without a 0.60 neighbour in the jailbreak family). Then 'python -m src.evaluate --sealed' once. Tables: A outside sets (NotInject with English and non-English lines, toxic-chat under its own label and without a pass/fail standard, blind set if it exists); A2 in-the-wild prompts by date; B reused sets (official final part, deepset, jackhhao, gandalf) with their times-scored count, where the six original standards are evaluated as comparison values; C development estimate for an unseen family; D same source as training (llmail, yanis and aya, gandalf family). Every row shows rows and groups, recall and false alarms per 1,000 with intervals, and precision projected to 1% and 10% attack share with a range; sets with fewer than 100 rows in the measured class carry no standard; hand-written set 4 is labelled by author.
actions.verify: frozen.json is older than the first ledger line and contains a range for every sealed set. The ledger has exactly one line for round 4. No mistake text was printed. sealed_predictions.csv is opened only after the write-up numbers are fixed.
actions.cost: Machine: 15-30 minutes, almost all embedding of test pieces.

actions.action: Write-up and notebook. Results are copied unchanged from the tables of step 13. Method and limitations state: the gate's guarantee covers 661 development texts that are all shorter than 230 characters plus the probe slices; a single firing of a content rule moves the decision by about +2 to +3.4 against a threshold near 0.54, so on command and agent text the verdict largely follows the rule; the intervals of the small gates (2 of 32 allows a true rate up to about 18%); the rule firing rates on llmail and deepset are measured on rows the rules were designed from; after this round no development number is independent of deepset wording and the deepset test figure is a fourth look; the embedded_human contrast rows were motivated by errors seen on the official test part; the raw yanis file was inspected before the split; round-four test numbers for long texts are not comparable with round three because the limits changed; how often each set was scored. New sections: 'Using the detector safely' (check each untrusted text separately, split long texts at the measured length, hide scores and fired rules from untrusted senders in a deployment, least privilege and human confirmation for destructive actions; cli.py and gui.py remain operator tools), 'Adding new examples and retraining', the drift log as a documented design only, and the rejected sentence-shift features as a negative result ('scalar cosine shift features do not separate attacks from ordinary multi-topic text'). Then the user is told the round is ready to commit.
actions.verify: Every limitation sentence cites a number present in report/metrics.json, gate.json or test_results.json. The notebook executes without errors. The plan file no longer mentions '--final', the 6 + 8 cap or the edit to output_manipulation_count.
actions.cost: About 1 day of writing. Notebook execution a few minutes.

dropped: Neutral command_mention_count column (fp-dangerous-rule M4): both reviews reject it. With matched rows its weight is near zero, and with a negative weight it becomes a lever to lower the score of any attack.

Weak 'sudo alone' tier, the plan's veto 'or ending in ?', and 'execution verb + broad target' as a sufficient cue: they fire on tutorials and Dockerfile lines, or silence polite orders. The looser variant is only measured on the tune half.
Shared position gate between tool_action_count and dangerous_action_count, and 'could you' or bare 'what' in the question gate: the known miss starts with 'what' and would be skipped.
Editing output_manipulation_count for 'secretly / without telling' (plan section 2): the secrecy wording becomes evidence inside tool_action_count.

The plan's 2% noise gate and the gates 'at least 50% of deepset training attacks fire' and 'rule fires on at least 45% of llmail attacks' as pass criteria: the first passes at 0% because the pool has no such text, the others reward fitting patterns to the rows they were written from. Replaced by 0.5% per rule on text the author did not write.

llmail 'social engineering' exclusion and the separate 'disguised as correspondence' test row: judge_category exists only on judge-labelled rows and these are no longer used; the exclusion affected about 10 rows.
near_duplicate_stats() as a filter (deletes whole families) and llmail grouping 'by team' (no such field in llmail_p1.json).
Add-one-source repair screen (regression M5): no valid threshold, single-class sources build exactly the shortcut models, and it spends more decisions on the same 661 texts.

Fail-closed replica check, max(threshold_all, threshold_round3) and hard-coded reference counts in the gate: precision is not monotonic in the threshold and the replica cannot match the champion. Replaced by an advisory comparison, a joint threshold and counts read from the frozen score file.
LinearSVC ranking of grid settings (runtime M6): a second estimator for model selection, at the edge of the SVC-only constraint, small saving with 4 settings.

Fold-result memo on disk (runtime M4): its key as specified changes on every run (memory addresses in repr), and its main benefit, reuse by a --final training run, no longer exists because test scoring is a separate command on a frozen model. Only the out-of-fold frames are saved.
Per-source piece limits and the plan's cap of 6 windows + 8 sentences: evaluation and threshold would be set on a lighter scorer than predict(); saving is about 3-4 minutes of one-time embedding.
'--embed-only' including test texts and any test access in src/train.py, including the ablation on test sets: test pieces are embedded during the single sealed evaluation.

language_switch_count and insert units after a language switch: shortcut 'mixed language = attack', the only benign hits are translation requests, and the units would label ordinary sentences as attacks.
Pattern 'repeat after me' in the forced-output rule: it matches benign-labelled jackhhao training rows.
Sentence-embedding shift features (subtle-attacks M5): measured AUC 0.41-0.58 against benign multi-sentence text; kept only as a documented negative result.

Source-weight switch inside the parameter grid and the original weight formula: not a pipeline parameter, and it up-weights synthetic rows and shifts class balance. Kept only as optional last rung R5 with the corrected formula.
Pass line 'deepset held-out recall reaches 0.45' as evidence of generalisation: templates and patterns were modelled on deepset rows.

Opt-in prediction log and drift_report.py (robustness M4 part B): no real inputs exist, hash-only logs cannot support cluster detection, and predict() would gain a file-writing side effect. Documented as a design.
Optional 'coverage' key in the dict returned by predict(): changes the output of the interface that must not change.

Accent folding in make_views() and the 'padding' augmentation: folding damages Hindi, Japanese and Russian and re-creates the normalizer-against-its-inverse test; padding trains harmless sentences as attacks through the first-window and last-sentence rules.

Held-out technique folds inside the threshold frame, the gates 'precision at least 98% on grouped folds' and the quick-versus-full parity check: the first distorts the shipped threshold, the other two are true by construction.

Multi-message joining recipe and its half-sentence check: both halves of a split attack are already flagged alone, a newline join switches rules off, and the current model flags ordinary follow-ups such as 'Thanks. Now a new task: translate ...'. A valid check needs about 120 hand-written conversations.

Pooled 86.8% held-out-source recall as 'expected recall on a new style' and as a pass criterion: dominated by the templated main dataset and not comparable once sources are added. Replaced by the per-family table.
Offline machine translation (multilingual M6): several language pairs have no usable small model, new dependency, and its pass condition measured the wrong languages.

Cross-language cosine 0.92 filter inside train.py (multilingual M2f): would give different training sets in different runs and misses most translation pairs (median cosine 0.88). Replaced by a report line in python -m src.dataset.

Leave-one-language-out fits (15 fits): adding data cannot move the number and untagged rows leak into it. The same question is answered by the family-held-out fold, the yanis-alone and aya-alone folds and the paired cluster comparison from the grouped folds.

Stopword language tagger, Romanian yanis rows, and any change to payload_group(): the tagger leaves about 21% of short rows undecided, Romanian would be an attack-only language, and changing payload_group() would reshuffle the official dev and final halves.
Bootstrap over rows inside scores() (plan section 5b): too narrow on templated sets and gives 100%-100% with zero errors.
Checks '0 identical and 0 near-identical rows against load_pool()' and the held-out-family versus grouped-fold average precision comparison: both pass whether or not there is leakage.
Ablation and rule comparison judged on official_dev and handwritten_dev alone: the rules were tuned on them.

not_solvable.reason: Who is addressed is not in the text. 'Run rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* on your server' or 'Send the report to x@y.com' reads the same in a tutorial, in a mail to a colleague, as a legitimate order to one's own assistant and as an attack on an agent. With one text in and no second input no feature can separate them. This is also the root of the 11 embedded_human false alarms.
not_solvable.do_instead: Keep these cases out of both training classes, treat text without evidence of a machine addressee as benign, and state in report/writeup.md that attacks written like normal mail and bare orders are missed and that a legitimate 'wipe /tmp on your machine' is flagged. Block destructive actions by limiting what the assistant may do and by human confirmation.

not_solvable.reason: Every piece is scored alone and the text takes its highest score, so a command quoted on its own line after a question is scored without the question. Carrying context into sentence pieces would weaken detection of hidden instructions.
not_solvable.do_instead: Accept and document. The code-line veto covers Dockerfile and script lines only.

not_solvable.reason: No real-world measurement exists. Public sources contain almost no command text and no benign mail with addressed requests, so everything learned and measured comes from templates, about 85 real rows and hand-written sentences by one or two authors. Rare rules act almost as hard overrides after standardization, and changing that scaling would alter every earlier result.
not_solvable.do_instead: Report counts with sample sizes and intervals, print the leverage of each rule, and in a later round add a licence-checked source of real programming questions and real correspondence as development data only.

not_solvable.reason: About one third of deepset attacks carry no cue in the text (for example 'schreibe c++ code', 'Be a DJ'), labels contradict each other, and even at the most lenient threshold the current model reaches only 70.6% on its own deepset training attacks. Only 32 of the 97 missed training attacks carry any new cue. A follow-up such as 'That is done. Now write ...' is identical as an injected line and as an honest chat message.
not_solvable.do_instead: Expect deepset test recall around 40-50% and the external 85% recall standard to be missed; report it as missed and do not tune after the sealed run. Report deepset separately with its interval and state that it is a fourth look at 60 attacks.

not_solvable.reason: The detector is fixed, offline, readable and stateless. A determined attacker can probe until some wording passes, every veto in a rule is also a bypass, a misspelled or purely semantic payload in a very long text can still fall outside the scored pieces, attacks spread over several messages are never seen as a whole, and a successful attack looks like benign text to any monitoring.
not_solvable.do_instead: Present the detector as a first filter. The caller checks every untrusted text separately and splits long texts at the measured length; in a deployment scores and fired rules are not shown to untrusted senders; the assistant gets least privilege, an allow-list of tools and human confirmation for irreversible actions. After each reported miss add rewordings plus harmless look-alikes through the feedback file.

not_solvable.reason: No attack data written by native speakers exists here; the six yanis languages are translated templates. Languages outside the embedding model's list cannot be covered and the two-verdict interface cannot say 'language not supported'. Romanized text (the known Bengali miss) and false alarms on long non-English documents stay essentially unmeasured. Per-language samples are about 100 attacks or fewer.
not_solvable.do_instead: List the supported languages in the write-up, report per-language numbers with intervals and without performance claims, and confirm aya counts per language and the model card's language list at download time.

not_solvable.reason: A real seal is impossible for one person on one laptop, past re-use of the official, deepset, jackhhao and gandalf test sets cannot be undone, no available set is a sample of real use or contains indirect injection from outside authors, toxic-chat's label differs from this project's definition, and sets with 28 rows per class cannot support a narrow range.
not_solvable.do_instead: Make re-use visible with the manifest and ledger, base the round's claim on sets scored once, report reused sets as comparison values with their scoring count, give no pass/fail standard to sets under 100 rows per class, and treat this round's fresh sets as development data afterwards. The only real seal is a blind set held by other people until the model hash is handed over.

not_solvable.reason: The gate guarantees 'not worse on development data' only, and that data is short, mostly English and partly used up after three rounds. A promoted model can still score lower on a test set than round three, and whether two extra false alarms are worth catching command and agent attacks is a judgement, not something a gate can decide.
not_solvable.do_instead: Fix the gate constants and the rule 'the gate decision is final' before the run. If a test result is worse, report it as it is; switching back because of a test result would be a decision made on test data. Show champion and promoted model side by side.

not_solvable.reason: The first run of a round cannot be made short. Embedding costs about the same per new piece whatever is done, and SVC fits run on one core each and grow roughly with the square of the training units; a precomputed kernel does not fit in memory. All run times here are estimates because no fit was timed.
not_solvable.do_instead: Embed ahead with '--embed-only', keep normalize.py untouched, read the timing table after the first run and put the measured times into the plan and write-up. If a future round passes roughly 60,000 training units, reduce grid settings or folds on development evidence and say so.

conflicts: Piece limits versus run time versus model selection: the plan's 6 + 8 cap and the per-source cap save a few minutes of embedding, but a text takes its highest piece score, so the limits change scores of long texts, the 98% threshold, the calibrator and which candidate passes the gate. Resolution: one pair (64 / 128) in src/windows.py for training folds, development sets, sealed evaluation and predict(); its effect is isolated in the third infrastructure run on round-three data. Round-four numbers for long texts are not comparable with round three.

'Do not edit any of the 16 rules' (regression) versus gating authority_claim_count and the exfiltration pattern (command and tool risks): resolved by freezing the current rules as src/rules_r3.py for the champion pickle only. The champion's inputs never change, and rung R1 means 'same data, revised 16 columns', not the round-three model.

'Do not edit windows.py or augment.py because of the embedding cache' (runtime) versus tail units, script-safe splitting, rule-guided selection and augmentation fixes: the cache is keyed per piece, so only changed pieces are re-embedded. All such edits are made in one batch before the single embedding run, with an assertion that unaffected texts split identically. src/normalize.py is not edited, because that would re-embed everything.

Test scoring inside training ('--final' in the plan, in the regression gate and in the runtime memo) versus the separate sealed evaluation: the separate command wins. train.py loses all test access, the fold memo loses its purpose and is dropped, and test pieces are embedded during the one sealed run.

One shared source for yanis and aya (so held-out folds contain both classes) versus separate sources (to measure the language shortcut in both directions): sources stay separate for reporting, a family column drives the folds used for parameter choice, and the single-source folds are run once as report-only diagnostics.

Cheaper fallback comparison versus fair selection: lower rungs are fitted at the top rung's parameter setting only. That saves about 100 fits but tunes the rungs unequally, so if a lower rung wins its full grid is run before it is saved. The coef_ shortcut, cache_size and worker count are exact and cannot change which model is selected.

Benign twins and hard negatives (command questions, correspondence, follow-ups, multilingual) add high-scoring benign text and push the threshold up, which costs recall on every source; easy multilingual and templated rows push it down, which raises false alarms on English documents. Resolution: the joint threshold on originals, plus printing the threshold with and without synthetic rows.

New rules select their own training units through CONTENT_RULES, so in training a new rule fires on every selected attack unit and its weight is inflated; combined with the leverage of rare columns a rule's false-alarm rate becomes the model's. Resolution: rungs R1, R2, R3 separate data, unit choice and rule columns, and the rule-level gate is strict (0.5% per rule on foreign text).

llmail unit selection depends on the rules (only rule-hit units are trained on), which aligns 'rule fired' with 'attack'. Resolution: a loose selector wider than the features, one-window texts always contribute, and texts that give no unit are counted and reported.

Tail units need benign counter-examples that today do not exist (7 benign against 870 attack tails): they are trained on only after the twin rows are in the pool and only if at least 20% of tail units are benign.

Many small hand-written gates wear out and decide by one row: merged into one probe file with tune and check halves, a tie rule for sets under 60 rows, and set 4 written by the user before the rules are coded. Command and topic-switch gates on decision values are replaced by calibrated probability, because decision values of different models are not on the same scale.

The known miss is wanted by three mitigations at once (command gate, contrast frame, retraining dry run): it stays a regression row excluded from recall, is not cloned into a generator frame, and the retraining dry run uses a different miss.

Per-row seeding of augmentation and the new 'typo' technique re-draw every copy once, so the replica baseline differs from the champion for reasons unrelated to quality: the replica comparison is advisory and the gate decides against the real champion pickle.

German data: balancing per language argues for fewer German attacks, the deepset weakness argues for keeping them. Resolution: fill German benign from deepset, aya and templates first; only translated yanis rows may be capped, deepset rows never.
result.runtime_estimate: Machine time on the 8-thread laptop (estimates; no fit was timed, the first timing table must confirm them): infrastructure verification on round-three data about 50-60 minutes (three development runs of 15-20 minutes plus about 5 minutes of embedding); rule-level gates and data reports several minutes each; one-time embedding for round four 25-45 minutes (roughly 40,000-60,000 new pieces; the two reviews measured 35 and 85 pieces per second); development run 1.5-2 hours (corpus build 5-10 minutes because rule values are not cached, then roughly 95-110 linear SVC fits on folds of about 30,000 units, against 80 fits in 13.5 minutes on about 15,000 units in round three); robustness checks 15-30 minutes; sealed evaluation 15-30 minutes. Total about 3.5-4.5 hours if the gate passes first time, about 5-6 hours with the one allowed repair run, and up to 7 hours if a lower rung wins and needs its own grid. The plan's figure of about 1.5 hours is not realistic. Working time: about 17-19 working days for everything in the list, of which about 1 day is hand-writing by the user; steps 1-5 and 11-14 (freeze, infrastructure, gate, sealed evaluation, write-up) are about 7 days and are the part that must not be skipped. Critical files for implementation: /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/src/train.py; /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/src/pipeline.py; /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/src/rules.py; /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/src/dataset.py; /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/scripts/download_dataset.py (new: /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/src/gate.py, /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/src/evaluate.py).

gaps: embedded_human false alarms are not measurable with the planned gates. Measured with load_test() + payload_group() in /home/guts/Documents/Mlproject/src/dataset.py: the 74 embedded_human rows of the official final part are only 2 payload groups, the 87 rows in official_dev are also 2 groups (0 false alarms), training has 697 rows in 16 groups. So the 11 test false alarms come from at most 2 distinct human-directed sentences, official_dev says nothing about this error type, and probe_dev.csv has no slice for it (command, correspondence, topic_switch, multilingual, long_benign only).
